_schema: Each row: id, class(live|filing|event), value, status(clear|amber|red|watch), proposed_status, rationale, confidence(high|medium|low), series_id, source, citation(URL), as_of(YYYY-MM-DD), next_release. RULES: (1) live/filing status is derived deterministically from value vs trigger. (2) event rows — the agent may self-promote clear->amber WITH a citation; amber->red and any de-escalation go in proposed_status for user confirm, never in status. (3) No citation => no status change on event/filing rows (the console rejects it). (4) confidence defaults to 'medium' if unstated. (5) reputable secondary sources (Reuters/BBG/FT) are acceptable when the primary isn't out yet.
_paste_note: The agent writes only the mutable fields (value, status, proposed_status, rationale, confidence, citation, as_of, next_release). The console holds the static definitions (names, conditions, guardrails, trigger). Paste this whole object, or just a {"asOf":..,"posture":..,"rows":[..]} with the ids you changed.

rows.trigger: RED: 2+ of MSFT/GOOGL/AMZN/META guide capex DOWN YoY. AMBER: AI credit stress (CDS/spreads widening) + compute/memory pricing rolling over together.
rows.value: no YoY guide-down — MSFT calendar capex ~$170B on 3P delays; GOOGL $195-205B unchanged, Cloud +103%; AMZN ~$220B unchanged, AWS +39%; META floor $135-145B
rows.rationale: All four have now reported. Red needs two or more guiding capex down year-over-year. None did. Microsoft, Oct 28 call: capex $45.2B in the quarter because third-party capacity deliveries slipped; calendar-2026 spend "approximately $170 billion" for that reason; Q2 capex over $50B; H2 spend expected to accelerate. Azure +48%, and Hood guided 49-50% constant-currency next quarter with demand still exceeding supply. CNBC describes the $170B as down from about $175B in July — one same-year trim on delivery delays, not a YoY cut. Alphabet, Oct 28: 2026 capex range $195-205B unchanged, 2027 expected significantly higher; Google Cloud +103% to $30.7B (TPU system sales a meaningful part; ex-TPU still described as very strong). Amazon, Oct 29: 2026 cash capex still about $220B, and Jassy said 2027 will be meaningfully higher; AWS +39%. Meta's Oct 21 floor raise to $135-145B stands. Amber pair not met: AI credit is stressed, but compute/memory pricing is not rolling over with it. A GPU-rental index shows H100 on-demand medians flat-to-up through Oct 31 (about $3.25-3.33), and a JPMorgan note dated Oct 26 (via TechFlow) has H100 rentals +6.5% MoM, B200 +4.7%, DRAM spot +4.4%, with only legacy A100 −3.5%. Token prices are not deflating: Hood cited higher revenue per token, and that note has October token spending +40% MoM with the weighted price +12%. CoWoS is not opening — the constraint is delayed 3P capacity. Circular-financing color is real (GPU-as-a-service delays, Alphabet turning to third-party compute, CoreWeave CDS still distressed) and it is not a guide-down.
